merger_description:
Armstrong Bidco, Inc. (**Bidco**) is a special purpose vehicle wholly owned by Armstrong Parent, Inc. (**Parent**) and indirectly majority owned by investment funds, vehicles and/or accounts advised and managed by various subsidiaries of KKR & Co. Inc. (together with its subsidiaries, **KKR**).

Bidco has no operational activities and was incorporated for the purpose of merging with and into Integer, with Integer remaining the surviving entity. Parent is indirectly majority owned by investment funds, vehicles and/or accounts advised and managed by KKR.

KKR is a global investment firm that offers alternative asset management as well as capital markets and insurance solutions. KKR sponsors investment funds that invest in private equity, credit, and real assets and had strategic partners that manage hedge funds.

Integer Holdings Corporation (together with its subsidiaries, **Integer**) is a medical device contract development and manufacturing organisation (**CDMO**) that provides outsourced medical device development, manufacturing, and related services primarily to manufacturers in the medical device industry.

Integer’s CDMO activities include the design, development, manufacturing, testing, packaging, labelling, storage, handling, distribution, marketing, and export of medical devices. Integer does not have a physical presence in Australia and its only activity in Australia is sales.

The acquisition relates to the indirect acquisition of a majority of the equity interests of Integer by Parent (the **Acquisition**).

Pursuant to an Agreement and Plan of Merger, by and among Integer, Parent and Bidco, Parent will acquire 100% of the equity interests of Integer. As such, following completion of the Acquisition, Parent will acquire control over Integer. At closing, pursuant to the terms of the Merger Agreement, Bidco will merge with and into Integer, with Integer being the surviving entity as a wholly owned subsidiary of Parent.

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition. In particular:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between KKR and Integer in the
supply of medical device contract development and
manufacturing services in Australia
b. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
effects resulting from exclusionary conduct post-acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
